findings.finding: VA OIG confirms Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat, a general-use AI chat tool, is provided to all VA staff department-wide.
findings.exact_quote: Microsoft 365 Copilot chat is a general use AI chat tool that the VA provides to all VA staff.
findings.source_title: Review of VHA's Use of Generative Artificial Intelligence (Preliminary Result Advisory Memorandum 26-00182-42), VA Office of Inspector General
findings.notes: VERIFIED against full PDF: the quote 'Microsoft 365 Copilot chat is a general use AI chat tool that the VA provides to all VA staff.' appears verbatim in footnote 4 of VA OIG memorandum 26-00182-42 (Jan 15, 2026). An independent VA OIG report states verbatim that VA provides Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat to all VA staff. This is a genuine department-wide deployment, not merely technical availability. Corroborates and strengthens the inventory field, which reported the Copilot family at 50,000+ for first-draft generation; the OIG language is broader ('all VA staff'). The report's own focus is a patient-safety concern: VHA authorizes both VA GPT and Copilot Chat for use with patient health information without National Center for Patient Safety coordination.

findings.finding: VA GPT, VA's internally built generative AI chat tool, is available to every VA employee and had roughly 100,000 users onboarded by late 2025.
findings.estimated_users: ~100,000 onboarded; available to every VA employee (~470,000)
findings.exact_quote: VA GPT is available to every VA employee
findings.source_title: VA leader eyes 'aggressive deployment' of AI as watchdog warns of challenges to get there, FedScoop
findings.notes: VERIFIED against full page: FedScoop carries 'VA GPT is available to every VA employee' verbatim (page text: 'VA GPT is available to every VA employee, he added.'). FedScoop quotes VA CAIO Charles Worthington that VA GPT 'is available to every VA employee.' The ~100,000-users-onboarded figure (estimated 2-3 hrs/week saved, 70%+ improved job satisfaction) surfaced in related reporting from the VA AI inventory page; the FedScoop article verbatim confirms universal availability but not the exact 100,000 count. VA GPT is on-network and ATO-covered; commercial public tools are largely blocked on VA's network. Of the five agencies here, VA shows the clearest universal rollout: two general-purpose tools (VA GPT + Copilot Chat) both deliberately offered to the entire ~470,000 workforce.

findings.finding: DHSChat, DHS's internally built secure generative AI chatbot, launched to all ~19,000 DHS headquarters employees plus select pilot users across ten operating agencies.
findings.estimated_users: ~19,000 (HQ) plus select pilot users across 10 components
findings.exact_quote: now available to all the roughly 19,000 employees at DHS headquarters and select pilot users across ten operating agencies
findings.source_title: DHS launches internal GenAI chatbot to leverage non-public data, Nextgov/FCW
findings.notes: VERIFIED against full page: Nextgov carries the quote 'now available to all the roughly 19,000 employees at DHS headquarters and select pilot users across ten operating agencies' verbatim. DHSChat launched Dec 2024 to ~19,000 HQ staff plus pilot users in the ten operating components. Against DHS's ~260,000 workforce that is partial coverage (~7% guaranteed access at launch, expanding via pilots). The article also notes 'thousands of employees will be able to leverage generative AI capabilities safely and securely using non-public data.' Distinguish: this is a deliberate rollout, but department-wide reach was not achieved at launch. Consistent with the inventory field's 10,000-50,000 to 50,000+ range, which likely also counts commercial Copilot Chat and the component tools NIPRGPT/CamoGPT/Ask Hamilton on top of DHSChat.

findings.tool_name: Commercial generative AI (ChatGPT, Claude, Copilot Chat)
findings.finding: Before DHSChat, DHS had spent a year allowing employees to use commercial generative AI tools on public information, training thousands of staff.
findings.exact_quote: Last year, we began allowing employees to use commercial generative AI tools like ChatGPT and Claude on publicly available information only; thousands of employees have now received training and use these tools to support their work.
findings.source_title: DHS's Responsible Use of Generative AI Tools, CSIAC (DTIC)
findings.notes: VERIFIED against full page, with correction: original HSToday URL still 403s; verified instead against the CSIAC/DTIC (.mil) republication of the same DHS material, which carries the quote verbatim. The original quote misattributed the verb: the actual text is first-person 'Last year, we began allowing employees...' (statement by Michael Boyce, Director of the DHS AI Corps), NOT 'Last year, DHS began allowing...'. exact_quote corrected and source_url switched to the corroborating .mil page. Establishes that DHS's commercial-AI program reached 'thousands' of trained employees before DHSChat, i.e. partial coverage and opt-in/trained-user gated rather than universal. Note FedScoop separately reported DHS later cut off access to commercial tools like ChatGPT; the commercial picture at DHS has shifted over time.

findings.finding: HHS made ChatGPT available department-wide to all employees effective September 2025 after granting it a FISMA-moderate ATO.
findings.exact_quote: The Department of Health and Human Services has made ChatGPT available to all of its employees effective immediately
findings.source_title: HHS rolls out ChatGPT across the department, FedScoop
findings.notes: VERIFIED against full page: FedScoop carries 'The Department of Health and Human Services has made ChatGPT available to all of its employees effective immediately' verbatim. FedScoop (Sept 2025) reports a departmentwide email made ChatGPT available to all HHS employees, following a FISMA-moderate ATO and the Trump AI Action Plan directive. This is a deliberate enterprise rollout. Caveat: the tool cannot be used with PII, PHI, classified, or export-controlled data, so 'available to all' means general-purpose drafting/summarization, not sensitive workloads. This finding postdates and extends the OMB inventory field (which reported 10,000-50,000 for the Microsoft 365 Copilot family and listed ChatGPT/Gemini/Claude); the public record now indicates substantially broader ChatGPT coverage than the inventory bucket implies.

findings.finding: NIH operates ChIRP, a secure GPT-4o-based generative AI environment for the NIH intramural research community.
findings.estimated_users: NIH intramural community (a subset of HHS)
findings.exact_quote: ChIRP currently uses the GPT-4.o LLM developed by the OpenAI company and made available through the NIH STRIDES enterprise Azure cloud environment managed by CIT.
findings.source_title: ChIRP: A ChatGPT Model for the NIH Intramural Community, NIH Intramural Research Program (The NIH Catalyst)
findings.notes: VERIFIED against full page, with source correction: the originally cited NCI/CCR bioinformatics page does NOT contain this verbatim sentence (it only says ChIRP 'leverages large language models' and 'Supports multiple AI models'). The verbatim quote was located on the NIH IRP 'Catalyst' article (Mar/Apr 2025 issue, vol 33 no 2), which carries the sentence word-for-word; source_url and source_title updated accordingly and confidence upgraded to high. ChIRP is a secure GPT-4o environment for the NIH intramural community, enabling work with sensitive/de-identified data. It is a sub-agency tool (NIH only), so partial coverage relative to HHS overall. The OMB inventory field referred to this as 'CHIRP'.

findings.finding: No public statement of department-wide deployment scale for a general-purpose AI chat tool at DOJ was found; the OMB inventory lists CoPilot use without a user-count bucket.
findings.notes: Searched FedScoop, GovExec, justice.gov, and Microsoft press for any DOJ enterprise Copilot/ChatGPT rollout with a seat count or 'available to all staff' statement. FedScoop's DOJ AI inventory coverage (2025: 315 use cases, 60% pilot, 18% deployed) and reporting on a DOJ IT-service-desk generative AI effort exist, but none state how many DOJ employees can access a general-purpose chat assistant. The OMB inventory field lists 'CoPilot' for calendaring/meeting summaries/email drafting with no user bucket. DOJ component chatbots are documented but component-scoped. Conclusion: DOJ has not publicly disclosed general-purpose AI access scale; coverage relative to its ~115,000 workforce is unknown.

findings.finding: USDA lists Microsoft Copilot among optional generative AI tools for trained internal employees, but no public source quantifies how many of its ~100,000 employees have access.
findings.estimated_users: subset of ~100,000 workforce; exact count not disclosed
findings.exact_quote: Grok will be available as an optional tool on the same basis as Copilot and OpenAI models for data analysis, scientific research, conservation planning, agricultural modeling, operational efficiency, and anything that trained internal USDA employees see fit.
findings.source_title: Agriculture Department plans to use Grok, despite growing concerns over the chatbot, Fast Company
findings.notes: VERIFIED via search corroboration: the Fast Company article URL still 403s to direct fetch, but a WebSearch returned the quote verbatim from that same Fast Company exclusive, so the quote text is confirmed against the source even though the live page is bot-blocked. It confirms USDA offers Copilot and OpenAI models 'on the same basis' as the newly added Grok, restricted to 'trained internal USDA employees' (i.e., gated by training, not universal). USDA's workforce is ~100,000 across 4,500 locations. The OMB inventory field reported Microsoft Copilot Chat at 50,000+ for knowledge retrieval, which would be roughly half the workforce, but no public source verifies that figure or states 'available to all employees.' Earlier USDA history (2023) shows it deemed public ChatGPT 'high' risk and stood up a Generative AI Review Board, so USDA's posture is governed/gated rather than open. Confidence kept low: quote/source verified, but the article is undated in the snippet and the 50,000+ inventory number is not independently corroborated.
